questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The wish to become closer to Poland and Polish culture, as well as becoming better in the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It a little difficult to figure out how to first get into the USOS system at the University of Warszaw, but after that it was very easy and approachable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an exchange coordinator who was terrific at answering any questions if needed, also we could be assigned a student to help us integrate in the beginning. I did however not take part in this offer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got my apartment through my Polish family. However, i very much recommend living in the Praga area, it was really nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Remember to be early about finding a place to live, and rent through the sites you are sent by the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite confusing in the sense that I didn't find it that clear which courses were available and which weren't. In the end it turns out they figured out which courses would be offered a month before the start of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The correspondence with the exchange coordinator was really helpful in this regard. The speed of getting an answer was really comforting in this confusion.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Many of the classes I wanted to take were either not on offer for the winter semester, or were at the same time as my mandatory courses. The courses I were able to register to, were however very good.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about figuring everything out before you arrive in Warsaw. There is time to change courses, and drop out during the first month. Also try to register to non-Erasmus courses, they are a lot more interesting. Just send the professor of the course you want to take an email. They are usually very friendly and appreciative if exchange students want to take their courses, and answer very quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a lot less structured and easier than what I have at UCPH. Many subjects were without a very concrete curriculum, and was instead just the professor talking. The exams were in many cases, especially in the Erasmus courses, just a 10 min presentation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot more focus on "class-participation" and we were graded based on this participation. This made for a weird forcefulness and stress for the students around trying to say as much as possible during class. This method, while well-intentioned, was more to the detriment of learning and participation than contributive.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: European Primary and Secondary Law, Decision-Making Procedures in European Union, European Institutions, Comparative Politics, Comparative Political Systems (I), Foreign Policy of Central and Eastern European Countries, Continuity and Change in American Society, Security Arrangements in Peace Processes: Theory and Practice, Evolution of the Welfare State: a Global perspective.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking European Primary and Secondary Law, Decision-Making Procedures in European Union, European Institutions, Comparative Politics, Comparative Political Systems (I) as they together cover the mandatory subjects for the Political Science exchange semester (DAK3 and EP). I also really recommend Foreign Policy of Central and Eastern European Countries and Evolution of the Welfare State: a Global perspective, as these courser are really interesting, with very knowledgeable and passionate professors which were really inspiring. Take Continuity and Change in American Society if you want to have the funniest subject you will ever have.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, its really easy to get it cheap at Milk Bars - Very recommended.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN at university of Warszaw had events three days a week, every week. A lot of different activities were on offer; from axe throwing, to polish practice to squirrel watching.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climbing at Crux is really cheap and nice. You can get into most museums by paying only 2 zloty as a student, and there are a lot of good ones: Zacheta, Polin etc. Cinema is also cheap and really good, i went once a week. Recommend going to Cinema Amondo.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Trains are pretty cheap for students and there are many really nice cities around Poland. I really recommend seeing Krakow and Gdansk for a weekend trip. It can also be really nice with a day trip to Lodz.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Polish people are very nice and friendly, as long as you act nice around them you'll be fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take non-Erasmus subjects.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more hierarchical relations, especially with professors.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Slavic hospitality.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy yourself. Don't take it too seriously, and enjoy all the cultural opportunities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of how much cheaper it is to eat out, do various activities, museums etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know how amazing of a country Poland is.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not eating out all of the time, it was nice and cheap.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
